rows.stem: The number of multiples of 6 lying between 25 and 363 is :
rows.solution:
The multiples of 6 between 25 and 363 are \(30, 36, 42, \ldots, 360\), an AP with \(a = 30\), \(d = 6\) and last term 360.

\(360 = 30 + (n - 1) \times 6\) gives \(n - 1 = 55\), so \(n = 56\).

This is option (A) \(56\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: A polynomial \(p(x)\), which has sum of its zeroes equal to their product, is :
rows.solution:
For \(ax^2 + bx + c\), the sum of the zeroes is \(-\dfrac{b}{a}\) and the product is \(\dfrac{c}{a}\).

For \(3x^2 - 2x + 2\): sum \(= -\dfrac{-2}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}\) and product \(= \dfrac{2}{3}\), so the two are equal.

(The others fail: \(3x^2 + 2x + 2\) has sum \(-\dfrac{2}{3}\) and product \(\dfrac{2}{3}\); \(3x^2 - 2x - 3\) has sum \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) and product \(-1\); \(x^2 - 3x + 2\) has sum 3 and product 2.)

This is option (C) \(3x^2 - 2x + 2\).

rows.stem: In the given figure, \(OA \times OB = OC \times OD\). Which of the following option is correct ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - that the segments AB and CD cross at O, with A and D on one side forming triangle AOD and C and B on the other forming triangle COB, is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
In the figure, AB and CD cross at O, with triangle AOD on one side and triangle COB on the other.

\(OA \times OB = OC \times OD\) gives \(\dfrac{OA}{OC} = \dfrac{OD}{OB}\).

In triangles AOD and COB, \(\dfrac{OA}{OC} = \dfrac{OD}{OB}\) and \(\angle AOD = \angle COB\) (vertically opposite angles), so \(\Delta AOD \sim \Delta COB\) (SAS similarity), with the vertices corresponding in the order \(A \leftrightarrow C\), \(O \leftrightarrow O\), \(D \leftrightarrow B\).

Corresponding angles are equal, so \(\angle A = \angle C\). (The similarity \(\Delta OAD \sim \Delta OBC\) would need \(\dfrac{OA}{OB} = \dfrac{OD}{OC}\), that is \(OA \times OC = OB \times OD\), which is not what is given.)

This is option (A) \(\angle A = \angle C\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: Equation of a line coincident with \(2{\cdot}5x - 2y = 3\) is :
rows.solution:
Write the line as \(2{\cdot}5x - 2y - 3 = 0\) and compare it with \(5x - 4y - 6 = 0\):

\(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{2{\cdot}5}{5} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{-2}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{-3}{-6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

All three ratios are equal, so the lines are coincident. (Multiplying \(2{\cdot}5x - 2y = 3\) by 2 gives \(5x - 4y = 6\) directly. The lines \(5x - 4y = 3\) and \(15x - 12y - 3 = 0\) are parallel to it, not coincident.)

This is option (D) \(5x - 4y - 6 = 0\).

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: In an A.P., the first term is 4 and the last term is 31. If sum of all the terms is 175, find the number of terms and the common difference.
rows.solution:
Here \(a = 4\), the last term \(l = 31\) and \(S_n = 175\).

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}(a + l)\), so \(\dfrac{n}{2}(4 + 31) = 175\), that is \(\dfrac{35n}{2} = 175\) and \(n = 10\).

The 10th term is the last term: \(a_{10} = 4 + 9d = 31\), so \(9d = 27\) and \(d = 3\).

There are 10 terms and the common difference is 3.

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: How many terms of the A.P. 21, 18, 15, .... must be added to get the sum zero ?
rows.solution:
Here \(a = 21\) and \(d = 18 - 21 = -3\). We need \(S_n = 0\):

\(\dfrac{n}{2}[2 \times 21 + (n - 1)(-3)] = 0\), that is \(\dfrac{n}{2}(45 - 3n) = 0\), or \(n^2 - 15n = 0\).

\(n(n - 15) = 0\), so \(n = 0\) or \(n = 15\). The number of terms is a natural number, so \(n = 15\).

15 terms must be added. (Check: \(a_{15} = 21 + 14 \times (-3) = -21\), and \(S_{15} = \dfrac{15}{2}(21 - 21) = 0\).)

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Determine the ratio in which the line \(3x + y - 9 = 0\) divides the line segment joining the points \((1, 3)\) and \((2, 5)\). Find the point of intersection.
rows.solution:
Let the line divide the segment joining \(A(1, 3)\) and \(B(2, 5)\) in the ratio \(k : 1\) at the point P. By the section formula,

\(P = \left(\dfrac{2k + 1}{k + 1}, \dfrac{5k + 3}{k + 1}\right)\).

P lies on \(3x + y - 9 = 0\), so

\(3\left(\dfrac{2k + 1}{k + 1}\right) + \dfrac{5k + 3}{k + 1} - 9 = 0\), that is \(6k + 3 + 5k + 3 - 9k - 9 = 0\), so \(2k - 3 = 0\) and \(k = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

The required ratio is \(3 : 2\).

Then \(P = \left(\dfrac{3 \times 2 + 2 \times 1}{3 + 2}, \dfrac{3 \times 5 + 2 \times 3}{3 + 2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{8}{5}, \dfrac{21}{5}\right)\).

(Check: \(3 \times \dfrac{8}{5} + \dfrac{21}{5} - 9 = \dfrac{24 + 21 - 45}{5} = 0\).)

The angle of elevation of the top of a building from a point A, on the ground, is \(30^\circ\). On moving a distance of 24 m towards its base to the point B, the angle of elevation changes to \(60^\circ\). Find the height of the building and distance of point A from the base of the building. (Take \(\sqrt{3} = 1{\cdot}73\))
rows.solution:
Let CD be the building of height h m, with C its base. Let B be the second point, with \(CB = x\) m, so \(CA = x + 24\) m.

In right triangle DCA:

\(\dfrac{h}{x + 24} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(x + 24 = h\sqrt{3}\) ... (i)

In right triangle DCB:

\(\dfrac{h}{x} = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), so \(h = x\sqrt{3}\) ... (ii)

Substituting (ii) in (i): \(x + 24 = 3x\), so \(x = 12\).

Then \(h = 12\sqrt{3} = 12 \times 1{\cdot}73 = 20{\cdot}76\), and \(CA = 12 + 24 = 36\).

The height of the building is \(20{\cdot}76\) m and point A is 36 m from the base of the building.

rows.stem: A tower stands vertically on the ground. A man standing at the top of the tower observes his friend at an angle of depression of \(30^\circ\), who is approaching the foot of the tower with a uniform speed. 30 seconds later, the angle of depression changes to \(60^\circ\). Find the time taken by his friend to reach the foot of the tower from this point.
rows.solution:
Let AB be the tower of height h m, with A its foot. Let D be the friend's first position and C his position 30 seconds later, with \(AC = x\) m and \(CD = y\) m. The angles of depression \(30^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) equal the angles of elevation of B from D and C.

In right triangle BAD:

\(\dfrac{h}{x + y} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(h = \dfrac{x + y}{\sqrt{3}}\) ... (i)

In right triangle BAC:

\(\dfrac{h}{x} = \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}\), so \(h = x\sqrt{3}\) ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), \(\dfrac{x + y}{\sqrt{3}} = x\sqrt{3}\), so \(x + y = 3x\) and \(y = 2x\).

The friend walks at a uniform speed and covers the distance \(y = 2x\) in 30 seconds, so he covers the distance x in \(30 \times \dfrac{x}{2x} = 15\) seconds.

The friend takes 15 seconds to reach the foot of the tower from the second point.
